newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end almost one percent weaker.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end almost one percent weaker.

text.p: * Toronto's key stock index lost almost one percent on Thursday as investors sold equities on the heels of a central bank rate hike. * 96 million shares traded worth C$1.8 billion.
In a surprise move, Canada's central bank boosted its influential bank rate to 3.5 percent, the first such hike in more than two years.

Katherine Beattie, MMS International analyst, said that higher interest rates provided competition for stocks as market players snapped up fixed-income instruments, betting that rates would go higher.
All of Toronto's 14 sectors dropped except for conglomerates. Transportation group shed the most points, followed by industrial products and interest-sensitive utilities.
Declining stocks beat out advancers 591 to 416, while 276 finished steady.

* Moore Corp Ltd fell 2.25 to 27.80 in trading of almost 2.5 million shares. The business forms maker said late on Wednesday that second-quarter and full-year earnings would underperform analysts' estimates.
Moore added that it would buy back up to 5.7 percent of its 88.3 million outstanding shares.
* Banks were also hit by the rate hike, with Royal Bank of Canada -- Canada's biggest -- down 0.55 to 62.55 in heavy trading.
* Business software company Cognos Inc fell 3 to 44 in light trading. Late on Wednesday it reported lower first-quarter profits after a writedown.
